source_title: Furniture Expert Nate Bartlett Explains Furniture Construction and Quality Checks in HelloNation
source_excerpt:
The Article Outlines Practical Ways Shoppers Can Evaluate Construction, Materials, Hardware, Upholstery, and Finishes Before Buying Furniture.
CHARLEVOIX, Mich. , Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- How can you tell if furniture is good quality before you buy it? HelloNation published an article featuring insights from Furniture Expert Nate Bartlett of Bartlett's Home Interiors in Charlevoix, Michigan, that answers this question.
The article explains that furniture can look impressive in a showroom while hiding weaknesses that become noticeable with regular use. Examining furniture construction, materials, and everyday function helps shoppers compare pieces more effectively before buying.
According to the article, a useful inspection begins with overall stability. Tables, chairs, dressers, and sofas should feel stable when you gently test them from different sides. Excessive movement, twisting, or uneven contact with the floor may point to weak connections or poor assembly.
The HelloNation article also describes how furniture joints can reveal important details about build quality. Secure joints should fit closely, with no large gaps, visible separation, or movement under normal pressure. Quality furniture construction may use dowels, mortise-and-tenon joints, corner blocks, screws, or other reinforced connections depending on the piece.
Fasteners provide another useful point of inspection. The article notes that staples and nails can serve practical purposes, but they should not provide the only structural support in areas carrying significant weight. Reinforcing corners and other stress points can improve long-term stability.
Materials should also be considered according to their intended use. The article explains that solid wood furniture can provide strength and repairability, while quality plywood and engineered wood can perform well when properly designed. The important factor is whether the material suits the structure and expected use of the furniture.
Drawers, doors, and hardware offer practical ways to evaluate workmanship. Drawers should move smoothly without binding, dropping, or shifting from side to side. Doors should remain aligned, while slides, hinges, handles, and other hardware should feel secure and operate consistently.
For upholstered furniture, the article recommends looking beyond fabric color and texture. Seams should appear straight and consistent, and patterns should align where appropriate. Cushions should support you and return to their original shape after you remove pressure, while the frame should stay stable during normal movement.
Finish quality can provide further clues. Wood surfaces should feel reasonably smooth, with stain or paint appearing consistent across visible areas. The article notes that natural materials may have small variations, but rough patches, drips, cracks, and poorly finished edges deserve closer attention.
The article also encourages shoppers to compare similar pieces side by side instead of relying mainly on price, appearance, or brand name. Testing stability, joints, drawers, upholstery, hardware, and finish can make differences in furniture construction easier to identify.
Furniture Expert Nate Bartlett's guidance supports the article's central point: furniture quality is best judged by several details working together. Secure joints, suitable materials, smooth operation, supportive upholstery, and careful finishing can provide shoppers with a clearer picture of how a piece may perform over time.
How to Tell if Furniture Is Good Quality Before You Buy features insights from Nate Bartlett, a furniture expert in Charlevoix, Michigan, in HelloNation.
